en.tldr: An output style is a set of instructions that shapes Claude's role, tone and response format for every response in a session. Pick a built-in style or write your own Markdown file. It is guidance Claude follows, not enforcement, and it doesn't replace CLAUDE.md for project knowledge.
whenToUse: Responses are consistently longer than you want: switch to Concise
You want the reasoning behind each change: Explanatory adds `Insight` blocks
You want hands-on practice: Learning leaves `TODO(human)` spots for you
Claude should act as something other than a software engineer: write a custom style
keyFacts: Built-in styles: Default, Proactive, Concise, Explanatory and Learning.
The `outputStyle` value is case-sensitive (`Explanatory`, not `explanatory`); the command ignores case.
Custom styles are Markdown files in `~/.claude/output-styles` or `.claude/output-styles`, with frontmatter `name`, `description` and `keep-coding-instructions`.
`keep-coding-instructions` defaults to `false`, which leaves out Claude Code's software engineering instructions.
The active style is sent with every request; a new style applies from your next message.
gotchas: A style is an instruction: nothing enforces it. Use a hook for something that must happen every time.
A mismatched `outputStyle` value silently gives you the Default style.
Style files are read at startup; restart Claude Code after creating or editing one.
Proactive doesn't change your permission mode; permission prompts appear as before.

confusedWith.difference: CLAUDE.md holds what Claude should know about the project; the style sets how it responds.
A hook runs deterministically at a lifecycle event; a style depends on Claude following it.
A skill loads for one kind of task; a style shapes every response.

questions.stem: A developer finds Claude's answers full of preamble, step-by-step narration and closing recaps. They want every response for the rest of the session to lead with the result, with the least setup, and without changing what their teammates get from the shared repo. What should they do?

options.text: Add "keep answers short" to the committed `CLAUDE.md`
options.why: `CLAUDE.md` is for project knowledge, and the committed file reaches every teammate.
Concise leads with the result and drops preamble, narration and recaps; the choice is saved to the local settings file.
Effort controls how much the model reasons, not the shape or length of its responses.

options.text: Relaunch with `--append-system-prompt` and a brevity instruction
options.why: It works for that launch, but you must pass it every time and restart the session.

questions.explanation: The requirement is about the shape of every response, with minimal setup and no effect on teammates. The Concise output style does exactly that, and `/output-style` saves it to `.claude/settings.local.json`, which is local to you. A committed `CLAUDE.md` would affect everyone, and effort changes reasoning depth, not response format.
keywordCues: every response for the rest of the session
without changing what their teammates get

es.stem: Un desarrollador ve que las respuestas de Claude traen introducción, narración paso a paso y resúmenes al final. Quiere que cada respuesta del resto de la sesión empiece por el resultado, con la menor configuración y sin cambiar lo que reciben sus compañeros del repo compartido. ¿Qué debe hacer?

options.why: `CLAUDE.md` es para conocimiento del proyecto, y el archivo commiteado llega a todo el equipo.
Concise empieza por el resultado y quita introducción, narración y resúmenes; la elección se guarda en el archivo de settings local.
El esfuerzo controla cuánto razona el modelo, no la forma ni el largo de sus respuestas.

options.text: Relanzar con `--append-system-prompt` y una instrucción de brevedad
options.why: Funciona para ese arranque, pero hay que pasarlo cada vez y reiniciar la sesión.

es.explanation: El requisito es la forma de cada respuesta, con mínima configuración y sin afectar al equipo. El output style Concise hace eso, y `/output-style` lo guarda en `.claude/settings.local.json`, que es local tuyo. Un `CLAUDE.md` commiteado afectaría a todos, y el esfuerzo cambia la profundidad del razonamiento, no el formato.

questions.stem: A developer writes a custom output style to make Claude's review comments terse. After switching to it, Claude still sounds right, but it no longer scopes changes carefully or verifies its work the way it did in the Default style. What is the most likely fix?

options.why: The location changes who can use the style, not which instructions it keeps.

options.text: Add coding rules to the style's `description` field
options.why: `description` is shown in the picker; it doesn't restore Claude Code's built-in instructions.

options.text: Add `keep-coding-instructions: true` to the style's frontmatter
options.why: Custom styles drop the software engineering instructions unless this field is `true`.
It only applies to plugin styles and makes them apply automatically; it doesn't keep coding instructions.

questions.explanation: Custom output styles leave out Claude Code's built-in software engineering instructions, such as how to scope changes and verify work, because `keep-coding-instructions` defaults to `false`. Setting it to `true` keeps them alongside the new tone. The file's location and the `description` field don't affect which instructions are sent.
keywordCues: no longer scopes changes carefully or verifies its work

es.stem: Un desarrollador escribe un output style propio para que los comentarios de revisión de Claude sean breves. Tras activarlo, el tono es el correcto, pero Claude ya no acota sus cambios con cuidado ni verifica su trabajo como en el estilo Default. ¿Cuál es el arreglo más probable?

options.why: La ubicación cambia quién puede usar el estilo, no qué instrucciones conserva.

options.text: Agregar reglas de código al campo `description` del estilo
options.why: `description` se muestra en el selector; no restaura las instrucciones integradas de Claude Code.

options.text: Agregar `keep-coding-instructions: true` al frontmatter del estilo
options.why: Los estilos propios dejan fuera las instrucciones de ingeniería de software salvo que este campo sea `true`.
Solo aplica a estilos de plugin y los activa automáticamente; no conserva las instrucciones de código.

es.explanation: Los output styles propios dejan fuera las instrucciones integradas de ingeniería de software de Claude Code, como acotar cambios y verificar el trabajo, porque `keep-coding-instructions` vale `false` por defecto. Ponerlo en `true` las conserva junto al nuevo tono. La ubicación del archivo y el campo `description` no cambian qué instrucciones se envían.

questions.stem: A team wants two things in a repo: Prettier must run after every file edit, deterministically, every time; and while onboarding, a new developer wants Claude to explain the choices behind the code it writes, without being asked to write code themselves. Which two should they use? (Choose two.)

options.text: A custom output style that says "always run Prettier after edits"
options.why: A style is an instruction Claude follows; nothing enforces it every time.

options.text: A `PostToolUse` hook that runs Prettier after edits
options.why: Claude Code runs the hook itself after each matching tool call, so it doesn't depend on Claude.
It also leaves `TODO(human)` spots for the developer to write code, which they don't want.
It adds `Insight` blocks explaining Claude's choices while Claude does the task.

options.text: A line in `CLAUDE.md` telling Claude to run Prettier
options.why: `CLAUDE.md` is guidance too; it doesn't guarantee the formatter runs.

questions.explanation: The formatting rule must hold every time, so it needs a hook, which Claude Code runs itself at a lifecycle event. Explaining choices is about the shape of responses, which fits the Explanatory style. Learning adds the same explanations but also asks the developer to write code. A style or `CLAUDE.md` line about Prettier is only guidance.

without being asked to write code themselves

es.stem: Un equipo quiere dos cosas en un repo: Prettier debe correr tras cada edición de archivo, de forma determinista, siempre; y durante su onboarding, un desarrollador nuevo quiere que Claude explique las decisiones detrás del código que escribe, sin pedirle que escriba código. ¿Qué dos deben usar? (Elige dos.)

options.text: Un output style propio que diga "siempre corre Prettier tras editar"

options.text: Un hook `PostToolUse` que corra Prettier tras las ediciones

Agrega bloques `Insight` que explican las decisiones de Claude mientras hace la tarea.

options.text: Una línea en `CLAUDE.md` que pida correr Prettier

Un estilo o una línea en `CLAUDE.md` sobre Prettier son solo guía.
